## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Puppharattajātaka* (Ja 147) is a narrative included in the Pali *Jātaka* collection. According to the commentary edited by V. Fausböll, the canonical verse opens with the line *Na idaṁ dukkhaṁ aduṁ dukkhaṁ* [Fausböll 1877]. The framing narrative is set at Jetavana, where the Buddha delivers the teaching in response to a love-sick or discontented monk (*ukkaṇṭhitabhikkhu*) who confesses his longing for his former wife (*purāṇadutiyikā*), claiming he cannot live without her sweetness [Fausböll 1877]. In the tale of the past, the protagonist perishes while lamenting over a woman and is reborn in hell (*niraye nibbatti*); in the identification of the birth (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that he himself was the sky-dwelling deity (*ākāsaṭṭhadevatā*) who observed the event [Fausböll 1877].
